The production facility manufactures two types of products (Product 0 and Product 1) using two machines (Machine 0 and Machine 1) over four time periods (Period 0 to Period 3). The demand for Product 0 in Period 0 is **22.28694038228271**, in Period 1 is **15.40553617195959**, in Period 2 is **16.19622794603683**, and in Period 3 is **23.77133167016131**. The demand for Product 1 in Period 0 is **16.51020937307772**, in Period 1 is **15.41395287058592**, in Period 2 is **23.98409764196543**, and in Period 3 is **18.84683167137874**.

A machine can only be started up for a product if it was not producing that product in the previous period.

The total production, inventory, and backlog must balance customer demand for each product in each period. Production quantities, inventory, and backlog must be non-negative. Production and startup decisions are binary (either 0 or 1). import pyomo.environ as pyo

DATA = {
    # ---- costs ----
    "setup_cost": 121.0782541217011,
    "startup_cost": 69.65555018358044,
    "hold_cost": {0: 1.196682091019819, 1: 1.146459407730801},
    "back_cost": {0: 7.384397449671641, 1: 6.58642780982885},

    # ---- demand[product][period] ----
    "demand": {
        0: {0: 22.28694038228271, 1: 15.40553617195959,
            2: 16.19622794603683, 3: 23.77133167016131},
        1: {0: 16.51020937307772, 1: 15.41395287058592,
            2: 23.98409764196543, 3: 18.84683167137874},
    },

    # ---- machine capacity per period ----
    "cap": {0: 63.4339018881536, 1: 67.51600987446864},

    # ---- startup time per machine (consumes capacity) ----
    "startup_time": {0: 7.917022863645049, 1: 7.682853596177669},

    # ---- sets ----
    "products": [0, 1],
    "machines": [0, 1],
    "periods": [0, 1, 2, 3],
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.P = pyo.Set(initialize=d["products"], ordered=True)
    model.M = pyo.Set(initialize=d["machines"], ordered=True)
    model.T = pyo.Set(initialize=d["periods"], ordered=True)

    # ---- decision variables ----
    # production quantity of product p on machine m in period t
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.M, model.P, model.T, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    # end-of-period inventory / backlog of product p
    model.I = pyo.Var(model.P, model.T, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    model.B = pyo.Var(model.P, model.T, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    # setup (production run) decision: machine m set up for product p in t
    model.y = pyo.Var(model.M, model.P, model.T, within=pyo.Binary)
    # startup decision: machine m starts product p in t
    model.s = pyo.Var(model.M, model.P, model.T, within=pyo.Binary)

    # ---- objective: setup + startup + holding + backlog ----
    def obj_rule(m):
        setup = sum(d["setup_cost"] * m.y[mm, pp, tt]
                    for mm in m.M for pp in m.P for tt in m.T)
        startup = sum(d["startup_cost"] * m.s[mm, pp, tt]
                      for mm in m.M for pp in m.P for tt in m.T)
        hold = sum(d["hold_cost"][pp] * m.I[pp, tt]
                   for pp in m.P for tt in m.T)
        back = sum(d["back_cost"][pp] * m.B[pp, tt]
                   for pp in m.P for tt in m.T)
        return setup + startup + hold + back

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # ---- demand satisfaction / balance (equality) ----
    def balance_rule(m, pp, tt):
        prev_inv = m.I[pp, tt - 1] if tt > 0 else 0
        prev_back = m.B[pp, tt - 1] if tt > 0 else 0
        prod = sum(m.x[mm, pp, tt] for mm in m.M)
        return (prev_inv - prev_back + prod - m.I[pp, tt] + m.B[pp, tt]
                == d["demand"][pp][tt])

    model.balance = pyo.Constraint(model.P, model.T, rule=balance_rule)

    # ---- machine capacity ----
    def cap_rule(m, mm, tt):
        return sum(m.x[mm, pp, tt] for pp in m.P) <= d["cap"][mm]

    model.cap = pyo.Constraint(model.M, model.T, rule=cap_rule)

    # ---- at most one product per machine per period ----
    def one_prod_rule(m, mm, tt):
        return sum(m.y[mm, pp, tt] for pp in m.P) <= 1

    model.one_prod = pyo.Constraint(model.M, model.T, rule=one_prod_rule)

    # ---- production linked to setup (tight big-M = capacity) ----
    def link_rule(m, mm, pp, tt):
        return m.x[mm, pp, tt] <= d["cap"][mm] * m.y[mm, pp, tt]

    model.link = pyo.Constraint(model.M, model.P, model.T, rule=link_rule)

    # ---- startup logic: s >= y_t - y_{t-1} ----
    def startup_rule(m, mm, pp, tt):
        prev = m.y[mm, pp, tt - 1] if tt > 0 else 0
        return m.s[mm, pp, tt] >= m.y[mm, pp, tt] - prev

    model.startup = pyo.Constraint(model.M, model.P, model.T, rule=startup_rule)

    # ---- startup time consumes machine capacity ----
    def startup_time_rule(m, mm, tt):
        return (sum(m.x[mm, pp, tt] for pp in m.P)
                + d["startup_time"][mm] * sum(m.s[mm, pp, tt] for pp in m.P)
                <= d["cap"][mm])

    model.startup_time = pyo.Constraint(model.M, model.T, rule=startup_time_rule)

    return model

    # back[p,t]: end-of-period backlog
    model.back = pyo.Var(model.P, model.T, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    # assign[m,p,t]: machine m assigned to product p in period t
    model.assign = pyo.Var(model.M, model.P, model.T, within=pyo.Binary)
    # setup[m,p,t]: a production run of p on m in t
    model.setup = pyo.Var(model.M, model.P, model.T, within=pyo.Binary)
    # startup[m,p,t]: machine m starts up for product p in t
    model.startup = pyo.Var(model.M, model.P, model.T, within=pyo.Binary)

        return setup_term + startup_term + hold_term + back_term

    # Balance: inv_{t-1} - back_{t-1} + production - inv_t + back_t = demand_t
    def balance_rule(m, pp, tt):
        prev_inv = m.inv[pp, tt - 1] if tt > 0 else 0.0
        prev_back = m.back[pp, tt - 1] if tt > 0 else 0.0
        production = sum(m.prod[mm, pp, tt] for mm in m.M)

                - m.inv[pp, tt] + m.back[pp, tt]) == d["demand"][pp][tt]

                       for mm in m.M for k in m.T if k <= tt)

                                      rule=demand_sat_rule)

        return sum(m.prod[mm, pp, tt] for pp in m.P) <= d["capacity"][mm]

        return m.assign[mm, pp, tt] <= m.setup[mm, pp, tt]

    model.setup_link = pyo.Constraint(model.M, model.P, model.T,
                                      rule=setup_link_rule)

    # Startup definition: startup >= assign_t - assign_{t-1}
    def startup_def_rule(m, mm, pp, tt):
        prev = m.assign[mm, pp, tt - 1] if tt > 0 else 0
        return m.startup[mm, pp, tt] >= m.assign[mm, pp, tt] - prev

    model.startup_def = pyo.Constraint(model.M, model.P, model.T,
                                       rule=startup_def_rule)

    # Startup time consumes capacity
    def startup_time_rule(m, mm, tt):
        return (sum(m.prod[mm, pp, tt] for pp in m.P)
                + d["startup_time"][mm]
                * sum(m.startup[mm, pp, tt] for pp in m.P)
                <= d["capacity"][mm])

    model.startup_time = pyo.Constraint(model.M, model.T,
                                        rule=startup_time_rule)

    return model
